summary: Quota reconciliation lag after org cap increase causing sustained 429s on long-lived streaming sessions
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reported large number of 429 responses for in-flight streaming websocket sessions following an organization-level quota bump (quota increase applied via admin console at ~2026-03-09T22:15Z). The increase shows in the console and new API keys/sessions are able to consume higher throughput, but long-lived connections that were open prior to the change continued to receive 429s until they disconnected and reconnected.

Impact:
- HorizonMaps (dedicated) experienced elevated 429 rates on streaming endpoints for ~2 hours during a heavy mapping tile backfill.
- Multiple long-lived sessions for their ingestion workers received repeated 429s and stalled, causing a backlog and delayed processing of ~80k events.
- Customer reports this caused missed SLAs for downstream pipelines.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool in us-west-2 (cluster id: dp-32a1).
- Token bucket based rate limiter with per-tenant windowing (default window 60s) and session-affinity for established websocket sessions.
- Customer was using multiplexed websocket connections (4 workers per host) and persistent session tokens renewed every 12h.

Steps to reproduce (customer-provided):
1) Start a long-lived streaming session connected before quota change.
2) Trigger org-level quota adjustment in Console (increase throughput).
3) Keep existing session open and observe 429s returned on subsequent requests for ~1-2 hours until session reconnect.

Observed behavior:
- New sessions established after quota change consume tokens at the new higher rate without 429s.
- Existing sessions appear to be limited by a stale snapshot of the token-bucket allocation taken at session start.
- Rate-limiter metrics show the tenant allowance increased, but per-session counters remained at pre-change levels.

Expected behavior:
- Quota increases applied in Console should be reflected immediately for all active sessions (or there should be clear documentation stating reconnect is required).

Immediate workaround provided to customer:
- Recommend reconnecting long-lived streams to pick up the new quota allocation (customer did and throughput resumed).
- As interim mitigation, we suggested horizontal scaling of worker hosts to spread per-connection quotas.

Investigation notes (support/SRE):
- Reproduced in staging with dedicated-tenant test harness. Observed token-bucket state stored in a session-scoped in-memory cache which is only refreshed on session handshake.
- Admin quota changes update the tenant-level bucket in Redis, but we do not push updates to active session caches. Long-lived sessions therefore continued to consult stale in-memory values until reconnect.
- Rate limiter implementation contains optimization to avoid frequent cross-node reads for performance; this optimization introduced the reconciliation lag on quota mutation.
- Relevant logs: rate-limiter debug shows "session_bucket_snapshot" timestamps matching session start time, and "tenant_quota_update" entries after the snapshot time.
- Dashboard links: https://metrics.redwood.ai/d/rls/rate-limiter?org=dp-32a1 (customer-visible metrics sanitized).

Root cause hypothesis:
- Session-scoped bucket snapshots are not invalidated when tenant-level quotas change. The design assumed quotas are stable or that sessions are short-lived; it did not account for admin-driven quota mutations during heavy long-lived streaming workloads.

Short-term remediation plan:
- Add a reconciliation path: when tenant-level quota changes are detected, publish an invalidation event on the quota-change channel so session nodes refresh snapshot for affected tenant IDs.
- Deploy a hotfix to staging that subscribes to quota-change channel and forces snapshot refresh for active sessions (PR reference provided).

Long-term fix considerations:
- Evaluate cost/perf trade-off of always consulting tenant-level bucket in Redis for every packet vs. periodic background refresh vs. event-driven invalidation.
- Update docs/console to indicate that quota changes may require reconnect for streaming clients until reconciliation is implemented.

Customer communication notes:
- Notified HorizonMaps via email (marcus@horizonmaps.com) of the workaround and that we are prioritizing a fix.
- Offered credits for the processing delay while fix is rolled out.

Next steps / owner action items:
- (Liam) Validate hotfix in staging and run the customer reproducer (due 2026-03-12).
- (SRE) Roll out event-driven invalidation to canary nodes and monitor 429 rate.
- (Docs) Add Console note about reconnect behavior for streaming sessions after quota modifications.

Resolution notes (so far):
- Hotfix deployed to staging 2026-03-12. Reproducer showed immediate refresh of session snapshots on quota change.
- Canary rollout started 2026-03-13 to 10% of dedicated pool nodes; initial telemetry shows ~90% reduction in sustained 429s for pre-existing sessions after quota change.

Follow-up references:
- Slack thread: #support-horizonmaps (https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C05ABC9)
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rls/pull/412
- Confluence runbook: Rate Limiter Reconciliation (link above)
